rationale: C14 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. Most distinctively, both proclamations use the same numbered two-part ownership mechanism: federally owned lands within newly described exterior boundaries are immediately incorporated, while nonfederal lands within those boundaries become monument lands only upon federal acquisition of title. They also share the same Antiquities Act authority, valid-existing-rights qualification, administrative-protection rationale, land-description structure, and nearly identical warning clause. C02 and C16 are related monument-enlargement precedents, but C14 is materially closer in both wording and operative architecture.

shared_material.child_excerpt: subject to valid existing rights, (1) the lands now owned by the United States within the exterior boundaries of the following-described tracts of lands are hereby added to and made a part of the Capitol Reef National Monument, and (2) the State-owned and privately-owned lands within those boundaries shall become parts of the monument upon acquisition of title thereto by the United States
shared_material.parent_excerpt: subject to valid existing rights, (1) the lands now owned by the United States within the exterior boundaries of the following-described tracts of land ... shall constitute the Sitka National Monument, and (2) the privately-owned lands within such boundaries shall become parts of the monument upon acquisition of title thereto by the United States
shared_material.explanation: This is a highly distinctive, nearly verbatim numbered mechanism separating immediate treatment of federally owned land from contingent treatment of nonfederal land.

shared_material.child_excerpt: certain adjoining lands needed for the protection of the features of geological and scientific interest included within the boundaries of the monument and for the proper administration of the area
shared_material.parent_excerpt: certain privately-owned lands adjoining the said monument are needed for the administration and protection thereof
shared_material.explanation: Both predicates justify boundary expansion through the paired needs of monument protection and administration.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Warning is hereby expressly given to all unauthorized persons not to appropriate, injure, destroy, or remove any feature of this monument and not to locate or settle upon any of the lands thereof.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Warning is hereby expressly given to all unauthorized persons not to appropriate, injure, destroy, or remove any feature of this monument and not to locate or settle upon any of the lands thereof.
shared_material.explanation: The warning provision is verbatim, reinforcing the broader match, though it is not sufficient by itself because similar warnings recur in monument proclamations.
